title: Character weight submodules and scalar extension of split-torus coactions
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $M$ an additive abelian group, and $A[M]$ the group algebra with basis $e^m$ of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Let $V$ be an $A$-module and $\rho:V\to V\otimes_A A[M]$ an $A$-linear map, where tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For $m\in M$ define the character weight submodule $V_m(\rho)=\ker(\rho-(v\mapsto v\otimes e^m))=\{v\in V:\rho(v)=v\otimes e^m\}$. For any commutative $A$-algebra $B$, scalar extension is as in [def-weil-module-base-change]; define $\rho_B:B\otimes_A V\to(B\otimes_A V)\otimes_B B[M]$ as the composite of $B\otimes_A\rho$, the canonical tensor-distribution isomorphism $B\otimes_A(V\otimes_A A[M])\simeq(B\otimes_A V)\otimes_B(B\otimes_A A[M])$, and the group-algebra isomorphism $B\otimes_A A[M]\simeq B[M]$ sending $b\otimes e^m$ to $b e^m$ on the last factor. Thus if $\rho(v)=\sum_i v_i\otimes h_i$, then $\rho_B(b\otimes v)=\sum_i(b\otimes v_i)\otimes\overline h_i$, with coefficients of $\overline h_i$ mapped from $A$ to $B$. These constructions are defined for every $\rho$; when $\rho$ is a coaction they are its character weight submodules and its extended coaction. There is no finiteness, projectivity, nonzero-ring or flatness hypothesis.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 3.1.9 proof (1), printed p.86: split-torus weight subbundles and formation under base change; their underlying module constructions, without any finite-projectivity hypothesis.
